Outlaw Survivors · weapons revamp · proposal, pass 134

Aim Where You Face

Every weapon fires all the time, roughly where the Outlaw faces. What is close and in front comes first. Melee becomes a slash you see, not a sword you hold, and bombs, sunlight and lightning land on random spots ahead. This page proposes how, weapon by weapon, with its mutations, its levels and its risks. Nothing in the game has changed yet.

"The core idea of the change is to make it so player has a bit more control over where they are shooting and to make it so the weapons are firing all the time roughly in the direction they are facing ... the enemies that are closer and happen to be in front of the Player have priority. Last time we did this it didn't really work partly because the melee weapons looked weird."Garry, 2026-11-08

How aiming works today

Each weapon chooses its own target, in any direction. The Outlaw's facing plays almost no part:

  • Nearest or strongest close (pass 48: distance over a weight of max HP, at most ×3): the guns, the Sabre, the Spear, the Big Mouth, the Guitarra, the Frisbee, the Rocket Pod, the Killer Bees, the Turret Buddy.
  • Thickest crowd: the Dynamite, the Molotov, Skull Rain, the Hammer, the Gravity Gun's throw.
  • Random on the screen: the Sun Scepter (near ones likelier), the Zap Beam.
  • Where he walks: Land Mines at his heels, Salt behind him, Orbit Saws round him.
  • Already his facing: the Boomstick (towards the nearest within 6 m), the Dragon's Breath, and the Jackrabbit Mines (2 m ahead).

On top of that, pass 73: a special, an Elite or the boss within 10 m is taken first by every weapon. And pass 54: only creatures on the screen are chosen. Moving decides where he stands; it never decides where he shoots.

Last time: pass 95's "Fire forward"

Pass 95 added a debug switch, off by default. Six weapons (Sabre, Spear, Hammer, Frisbee, Tumbleweed, Basketball) fired along the facing until a creature stood within 75% of their range, then aimed as before. What went wrong, read from the code and the history:

  1. It was a switch, not an aim. The Sabre's 75% is 1.95 m. It swung at empty air until a goblin was almost touching him, then snapped to that goblin, often beside or behind him. From one stroke to the next the swing jumped between the facing and the target.
  2. The melee weapons are props. The blade is a 3D model that grows out of the painted Outlaw (left). Swinging at nothing, it reads as a sword sticking out of him, and when he turns it cuts through his own figure. An effect (a slash, a streak) reads as an attack even in empty sand; a prop only reads as a prop.
  3. Half the build did not follow. The other 18 weapons kept aiming all round, so the player's walking steered some weapons and not others. There was no rule to learn.
  4. Nothing showed the aim. No mark on the sand said where the weapons would go.
  5. Misses looked like mistakes. A Basketball with nobody to hit dropped to the sand; a Hammer smashed empty sand 3.45 m ahead.
  6. It was never measured. Off by default and locked off in the production build, it never went through the sim or the difficulty probe.

This time: one rule for every weapon; a cone with a soft assist instead of a switch; melee drawn as effects; a visible aim mark; misses that look meant (the ball comes home, the slash still flashes); measured with the sim before Garry plays it.

The shared rules

Numbered so the weapons below can point to them. Every number is a starting value to tune, kept in data.

  1. R1The aim line is his facing

    While he moves, the facing is the stick's direction (it already turns fast: about a quarter turn in a tenth of a second). While he stands, it stays where it was. Proposed addition: a turn-on-the-spot zone. A stick pushed less than 15% of its reach turns him without walking. That lets a standing player aim, which matters for Steady Hand, the Pressure Cooker and Held Breath. Garry decides (Q1).

  2. R2"Roughly" is a cone

    Each weapon has an aim cone (data: aim.cone, its full angle) centred on the facing and as long as its range. Starting values: 60° for aimed weapons (±30°), the weapon's own swing for melee (the Sabre's 150°), a 100° fan for placed weapons (±50°). The cone does not grow with area or level: area already grows what a hit covers. Named mutations may widen it (Sweep Fire, Far Reach, Wide Sweep). A creature counts as inside when its body touches the cone, so a big creature at the edge counts.

  3. R3A soft assist, not a lock

    Inside the cone a shot turns to the best target (R4), never more than the half cone. With nothing in the cone the shot goes straight down the facing. In a volley the first round goes at the best target and the rest fan round it as they do today.

  4. R4The score: near and in front first

    Every creature in range and in the cone (on the screen, standing, not still rising out of the sand: today's rules) gets a score, and the lowest wins:

    score = d × (1 + 2·(φ/θ)²) / w d distance in metres φ angle off the facing, θ the half cone w 1, or for a "strongest close" weapon pass 48's max HP over the crowd's mean (1 to 3)

    Worked with a 30° half cone: a goblin straight ahead at 6 m scores 6.0. One at 3 m but 25° off scores 7.2, so the one straight ahead wins although it is twice as far. One at 3.4 m and 12° off scores 4.5 and beats both. Behind him nothing scores.

    Pass 73's priority stays, inside a wider cone. A special, an Elite or the boss within 10 m is taken first if it stands within 1.5× the half cone (±45° for a gun). Turning roughly towards an Elite makes every weapon go for it; one behind him waits until he turns. Garry decides (Q6).

  5. R5Always firing

    On its clock every weapon fires down the facing even with nothing in the cone: the round flies its range, the slash cuts air, the bomb lands on sand. Exceptions carry aim.hold and wait for something to stand in the cone: the Dragon's Breath (up to 2 s, as today: a 10.6 s cooldown is too slow to waste), the Gravity Gun (it cannot lift air) and the Big Mouth (up to 0.5 s). It gives a rhythm the player can read and play with, shots ahead of a pack before it arrives, and bombs that clear the path. It costs damage spent on nothing (in quiet stretches a third of the shots or more), more rounds in the air, more noise; a dry shot can sound at half volume. One conflict: in pass 53 Garry asked the Boomstick not to fire when nobody is in reach until it is evolved (Q3). May's Trigger Happy loses its point (see the Tommy Gun).

  6. R6Placed weapons land in a fan ahead

    A placed weapon draws its spots in a fan: ±50° of the facing, from 2 m to its range. It draws six candidate spots from the run's dice, scores each by what its blast would catch (creatures in its radius; specials, Elites and the boss count ×3; the Dynamite's lead prediction stays as the scorer), takes the best 60% of the time, otherwise one of the other five. Spots of one volley keep 1.5 blast radii apart (today's claimed spots). With nothing ahead the spots land on empty sand in the fan, never behind. Random, leaning to the crowd, always in front. A ring all round weighted to the front is the alternative (Q4).

  7. R7The aim is shown

    A faint wedge on the sand in front of him (his widest aimed cone, 3 m long, about 12% opacity) that brightens for a tenth of a second when a weapon fires, and a small chevron at his feet. A Settings switch "Show aim", on by default (Q9). Placed weapons already show their spots (the Sun Scepter's rings, the fuse sparks).

  8. R8The PC plays the same game

    Keys set the facing in eight directions, 45° apart; with a 60° cone those eight cover the whole circle. No mouse aim for players: the phone has one thumb, and the analytics compare phone and PC runs. A mouse-aim row in the developer menu for testing only (Q8).

  9. R9The bot learns to aim by moving

    Today's bot legs (BotLegs, pass 62's kiting autopilot) circle-strafe: they keep the nearest creature a few metres off and drift sideways round the crowd. So the bot's facing is mostly 90° off the crowd: outside every cone. Under the new rule it would lose most of its damage, and the sim would call every stage too hard. The bot needs:

    • an attack lean: its steer blends the escape direction with the direction of the best-scored pack, so the crowd stays within ±30° while it backs off or arcs round;
    • turn-and-fire beats: every 1.5 to 3 s, a 0.3 s turn to the thickest front (with R1, on the spot);
    • a skill dial aim 0 to 1 in the presets (careless low, expert high), so the sim can show what a poor aimer and a good one each feel.

    The sim's numbers change for two reasons at once: the rule and the bot. Measure in that order: the old rule with the new bot first (it must match today's numbers), then the new rule with the new bot. The Watch shows the aim wedge and a "dry shots %" line.

Three families, and two that stay

Aimed

Fire down the facing; a soft assist inside a 60° cone picks the best target by the score. With nothing there the shot still goes. Revolver, Tommy Gun, Boomstick, Basketball, Frisbee, Tumbleweed, Big Mouth, Guitarra, Dragon's Breath, Gravity Gun, Rocket Pod, Killer Bees.

Melee as effects

No weapon in his hand. The Sabre is a crescent swing arc just above the sand: a bright steel edge with a soft smear, 150° wide × area, as deep as its reach, alternating left and right with each swing. The Spear is a thrust streak: a narrow lance of light to its full reach with a tip flash, the lane it hits drawn exactly. Mutations change the effect's edge, colour and count (a razor hairline, a gold flick, a red-hot fourth thrust). The effect costs one mesh a stroke.

Placed

Spots in a fan ahead (R6): random, leaning to the crowd. Dynamite, Molotov, Skull Rain, Sun Scepter, Zap Beam (its first strike; the chains still jump anywhere), Hammer, Land Mine (flicked ahead), Turret Buddy (set down ahead).

Around him: unchanged

Orbit Saws circle him and Salt trails behind him. Neither aims, and both already cover every side. Under the new rule they become the guard for his back, so their pick rates will climb.

Family

Aimed

Twelve weapons fire down his facing. A soft assist turns a shot to the best target inside the cone; with nothing there the shot still goes, straight ahead.

Revolver

Aimedeffort: small code

Today

A revolver floats beside him and fires a burst (1 round, 3 by level 5) at the strongest close creature within 14 m, in any direction. Rounds pierce once and fan 7° apart.

Proposal

The burst goes down his facing. Inside a 60° cone the first round turns to the best target by the score (R4); the other rounds fan 7° to either side of it as now. Nothing in the cone: the burst flies straight down the facing and is spent at 14 m.

cone 60° (±30°)big game cone ±45°fires dry: yes

Levels under the new aim

  • L2 +25% damage, −17% cooldown
  • L3 +1 pierce, +1 amount, −8% cooldown
  • L4 +30% damage
  • L5 −12% cooldown, +1 amount

Damage and cooldown steps play as today. The extra rounds at levels 3 and 5 fan out round the aimed round, so a full revolver covers about ±10° more of the cone. Pierce at level 3 rewards lining up a queue of creatures down the facing.

Mutations and evolution

Silver Bullet mutation

+50% damage and +1 pierce, in rounds half again as big that hit wider.

New aim: Rounds half again as big forgive a near miss: the best pick for a player who aims loosely.

Change: None.

Trick Shot mutation

A round that kills bounces on to the next enemy at 80%, every time.

New aim: The bounce after a kill goes to the nearest creature from the kill, in any direction. It stays that way: the chain is the reward for aiming the first round.

Change: None.

Hip Shot mutation

Every fifth pull fires three volleys 0.12 s apart, each the full round count, then the revolver spins.

New aim: Each of the three volleys reads his facing again when it leaves, so turning during the 0.24 s string sweeps it across a pack.

Change: Small: _hip_volley takes the aim line instead of the stored _aim_dir.

Golden Revolver evolution

Every round a silver bullet that ricochets twice at 80% without needing a kill; every third pull is a hip shot; every shot leaves a line of golden energy in the air.

New aim: The two free ricochets go anywhere, so the evolution feels forgiving at the end of a run, which is the right way round.

Change: None beyond the shared aim.

How it differs for the player

  • He has to point the gun. A goblin behind him is no longer shot until he turns.
  • The gun fires on every beat, so the rhythm is visible even in an empty patch of sand.

Risks

  • Low. 14 m and 60° cover most of the screen ahead of him.
  • Starting weapon of the Drifter, the first Outlaw: a new player meets the rule here. The aim wedge (R7) has to be on from the first run.

Tommy Gun

Aimedeffort: small code

Today

A Tommy Gun floats beside him and sprays a burst of 6 rounds (12 by level 4) in an 8° spread at the strongest close creature within 12 m. Rounds pierce twice.

Proposal

The burst sprays down the facing with its 8° spread. The first round of a burst turns to the best target in a 60° cone; every later round reads the facing again, so turning while it fires hoses the cone like a garden hose.

Levels under the new aim

  • L2 +2 amount, +25% damage, −8% cooldown
  • L3 +2 amount, +25% damage, −8% cooldown
  • L4 +2 amount
  • L5 −12% cooldown, +30% damage

Levels 2 to 4 add rounds to the burst: under the new aim that is a longer sweep, not only more damage. Damage and cooldown steps as today.

Mutations and evolution

Mini Crits mutation

A quarter of the rounds are mini crits: half a crit's extra damage, carried through every pierce.

New aim: Unchanged.

Change: None.

Sweep Fire mutation

The burst fans across 70° instead of a line.

New aim: Fits the new aim best of any mutation: the burst already fans across 70°, about the width of the cone, so one burst sweeps the whole front.

Change: None.

Drum Mag mutation

Twice the burst, −35% a round.

New aim: A burst twice as long gives more time to sweep while it fires.

Change: None.

Trigger Happy May's Outlaw mutation

The Tommy Gun never stops firing, even with nobody in range: a steady stream of two thirds more rounds, each 35% weaker.

New aim: Today it is the one weapon that fires with nobody in range. Under the new rule every weapon does, so its point is lost. Keep the stream (+2/3 rounds, 35% weaker each) and let the stream sway ±12° on its own, so May paints the cone without turning.

Change: Small code and new card words.

Chicago Typewriter evolution

Every letter is a bullet.

New aim: Chicago Typewriter's 14 rounds a burst with pierce 3: the sweep becomes a wall of lead down the facing.

Change: None.

How it differs for the player

  • The cone fills with tracers where he looks: easy to read.
  • A burst no longer chases a creature that walked round behind him.

Risks

  • Dry bursts are many rounds: 12 to 14 tracers a second flying their full 12 m with nothing to hit. Tracers are one MultiMesh, so this is cheap, but the projectile pool fills faster in quiet stretches.
  • May's Outlaw mutation must be reworded (above).

Boomstick

Aimedeffort: small code

Today

Already the one gun that fires 'forward': 5 pellets (8 by level 3) in a 35° cone towards the nearest creature within its 6 m reach. It does not fire when nobody is within reach (Garry, pass 53).

Proposal

The pellets leave along the facing in their own 35° spread; a small assist (±15°) turns the blast to the best target. The question is the dry shot: Garry asked in pass 53 that the Boomstick should not fire all the time until it is evolved. The new rule says every weapon fires on its clock.

More pellets at levels 2 and 3 fill the same 35° more densely; knockback at 4 and pierce at 5 as today. The short reach makes facing matter more than for any other gun.

Mutations and evolution

Dragon Shells mutation

Pellets set 60% of the enemies they hit on fire.

New aim: Unchanged.

Change: None.

Both Barrels mutation

Every third shot fires twice: a second blast right after the first.

New aim: Unchanged: the second blast follows the facing of the moment.

Change: None.

Birdshot mutation

No pellet flies loose: everything in a 2.6 m wide lane a quarter longer than the range takes 40% of a full point-blank volley at once and is knocked down the lane.

New aim: The 2.6 m lane a quarter longer than the range becomes the aim line itself: a clean fit, the player sees exactly what it covers.

Change: Data: the lane runs along the facing instead of towards the nearest creature.

Blunderbuss evolution

A bell for a mouth: everything in a 75° cone out to 10 m takes 30% of the whole volley at once, burns, and is thrown back; every second shot fires twice.

New aim: Blunderbuss already fires blind on its clock (fire_blind): it is the model for the rest. Its 75° cone to 10 m covers the front.

Change: None.

How it differs for the player

  • The shotgun now always points where he walks: walk into a pack to blast it.
  • If the dry shot is allowed, it bangs on every beat in empty sand.

Risks

  • Conflicts with Garry's pass 53 words if it fires dry. Option: fire dry at half volume, no screen kick.
  • 6 m reach and a 35° spread: the most dry shots of all guns while kiting.

Basketball

Aimedeffort: small code

Today

Fadeaway's ball is thrown at the strongest close creature within 9 m, bounces to others (1, then 3 bounces), and comes back to his hand: a catch refunds 35% of the cooldown and builds Heat.

Proposal

Thrown down the facing with a ±30° assist. A throw that hits nothing does not drop to the sand as in pass 95 (that read as a fumble): it flies its 9 m, takes a bounce if anything is within 7 m of its end, and else comes back to his hand. A dry catch refunds the cooldown but gives no Heat, so Heat still means hits.

cone 60° (±30°)dry throw returnsHeat only from hits

Levels under the new aim

  • L2 +25% damage, −17% cooldown
  • L3 +1 amount, +20% speed, −8% cooldown
  • L4 +30% damage
  • L5 +1 amount, −12% cooldown

Bounces at levels 3 and 5 still go to the nearest creature from the last hit, any direction. Speed +20% at level 3 makes the dry return quicker.

Mutations and evolution

On Fire mutation

He's on fire: everything the ball touches catches fire.

New aim: Unchanged.

Change: None.

Rebound mutation

The ball hits everything on its way back to his hand, at full damage and faster.

New aim: The way back is the same line as the way out, so Rebound doubles the hits down the facing. Stronger than today.

Change: None.

Alley-Oop mutation

Each hit has a 15% chance to throw the creature into the air. It can't attack up there and takes the hit again when it lands.

New aim: Unchanged.

Change: None.

Free Throw Fadeaway's Outlaw mutation

Every hit he evades throws a free ball at once, no cooldown. At most one every 0.8 s.

New aim: A free ball after an evaded hit goes at the creature he evaded, wherever it stands: the one exception to the cone, and readable as a counter.

Change: Small: the free throw passes its target instead of asking the aim.

Slam Dunk evolution

He catches. He dunks. The floor remembers.

New aim: Slam Dunk: 3 bounces with a 10 m reach and the dunk at 10 Heat. Hits keep Heat, dry catches do not.

Change: None beyond the dry-catch rule.

How it differs for the player

  • The ball goes where he looks and always comes home; no more balls lying in the sand.
  • Heat builds slower for a player who throws at nothing.

Risks

  • Heat farming: if dry catches gave Heat, a player could throw at air for free Heat. The rule above closes that.
  • Fadeaway's identity is the catch rhythm: keep the refund on dry catches or he feels slow.

Big Mouth

Aimedeffort: small code

Today

A floating mouth opens every 3.8 s, locks on the nearest creature within 13 m and pours a 2 s beam through everything on that line.

Proposal

The beam pours down the facing and follows it while it pours, at most 90° a second so it does not jitter. At the start it snaps to the best target within ±25°. The player steers the laser: that is the fun of this weapon under the new aim. It waits up to 0.5 s for something to stand in the cone, then pours anyway.

Duration +0.4 s at level 2 and +0.5 s at 5 mean longer sweeps; +3 m range at level 4 a longer line.

Family

Melee as effects

The Sabre and the Spear stop being props. Each stroke is drawn as an effect over the sand: a swing arc, a thrust streak.

Sabre

Melee as effectseffort: new behaviour

Today

A 3D sabre blade grows out of him and swings a 150° slice at the strongest close creature within 2.6 m; level 3 and 5 add swings that go left, right, left. A crescent trail follows the edge.

Proposal

No blade. Each swing is a crescent swing arc drawn just above the sand in front of him: a bright steel edge with a soft white smear behind it, 150° wide and as deep as the reach, sweeping across in 0.16 s and fading in 0.12 s. The arc is centred on his facing, turned up to ±20° towards the best target. It swings on every beat, creature or not. The hit test is today's slice (the edge passes each creature once a swing).

arc 150° × areadepth = reach 2.6 massist ±20°, swings dry

Levels under the new aim

  • L2 +25% damage, +20% reach, −8% cooldown
  • L3 −19% cooldown, +1 amount
  • L4 +25% damage
  • L5 +20% reach, +1 amount

Level 2: +25% damage and the arc 20% deeper. Level 3: a second arc, the other way. Level 4: +25% damage. Level 5: the arc another 20% deeper (3.7 m) and a third arc. The width of the arc is the slice angle × area, so Reach and other area items show on the arc itself.

Mutations and evolution

Critical Thinking mutation

+10% critical hit chance for every weapon.

New aim: The arc's edge becomes a razor-white hairline with a faint halo; a swing that crits draws today's white streak across the creature.

Change: Look: pass 61's LookRazor moves from the blade to the arc's edge.

Riposte mutation

Strokes come 25% faster and throw what they hit twice as far.

New aim: A brass-gold edge, and at the end of each swing a short reverse flick smear with a clang spark.

Change: Look: LookGuard becomes the gold edge; the flick is drawn as a small arc.

Flurry mutation

Twice the slices a stroke.

New aim: Twice the swings: arcs come in pairs, the second 10° turned and a little smaller, so the front flickers with steel.

Change: None (amount of swings).

Whirlwind evolution

Every swing is a full circle, four a stroke; a swing that crits refunds 20% of the cooldown. Flurry doubles the swings, Riposte speeds them and Critical Thinking's crits refund them: it hardly stops spinning.

New aim: Whirlwind: a full 360° ring of pale-cyan wind, four a stroke. It hits all round him, so the aim no longer matters; the evolution is the release from the rule.

Change: Look: the ring is drawn by the same arc effect at 360°.

How it differs for the player

  • He sees a slash every beat, so the sword reads as an attack even in empty sand, which the floating blade never did.
  • Only what is in front of him is cut. Backing away from a crowd cuts nothing.

Risks

  • The most aim-sensitive weapon in the game: 2.6 m and in front. Kiting players will feel it is weak; the sim must check its pick rate and kills.
  • Readability: an arc about every second across the front (faster with attack speed) can hide the creatures under it. Keep the smear soft (about 35% alpha) and only the edge bright.
  • Performance: one effect mesh a swing, a handful alive at once: cheap.

Melee as effectseffort: new behaviour

Today

Ironwood's 3D spear thrusts out of him at the strongest close creature within 4.6 m, 0.55 m wide, with a streak behind the tip and sparks where it bites. Level 5 adds a second spear fanned 40°.

Proposal

No spear. A thrust streak: a narrow lance of light shoots from his chest down the facing to the full reach in 0.1 s, holds 0.1 s with a sharp tip flash at its end, and fades in 0.3 s. The lane it shows (0.55 m × the reach) is exactly what it hits. A ±15° assist turns it to the best target, so the creature must be roughly ahead.

lane 0.55 m × reach 4.6 massist ±15°thrusts dry

Level 2: +25% damage, faster. Level 3: the streak 20% longer (5.5 m) and +30% knockback. Level 4: +25% damage. Level 5: a second streak, the two fanned 40° apart round the facing.

Every hit has a 15% chance to stun for a second.

New aim: A small yellow ring pops on each creature it stuns.

A 120° sweep like a sabre's, with less knockback.

New aim: The streak sweeps across 120° like the Sabre's arc, but narrow and tipped: a fan of light with a point.

Change: Look: the sweep is drawn with the Sabre's arc effect in the spear's colour.

+40% reach, strokes 15% slower.

New aim: A streak 40% longer (6.4 m): a sniper's lane.

Heartseeker Ironwood's Outlaw mutation

Every 4th thrust is a guaranteed crit and reaches 20% further.

New aim: Every 4th thrust is a guaranteed crit that reaches 20% further: the streak warms orange over the three before and the 4th is red-hot, thicker, with a red tip flash. Garry's own words for it (pass 62) already describe an effect, not a weapon.

Change: Look: LookCrit's red becomes the streak's colour.

Thunder Lance evolution

Every stroke is a 140° sweep of two lances and, straight after it, a thrust that throws half again as far. Every hit stuns for 0.8 s, and a stunned enemy takes ×1.5 from the lance: the sweep stuns, the thrust punishes.

New aim: Thunder Lance: a 140° sweep of two lances, then a thrust that throws half again as far; stuns make the thrust hit ×1.5. Drawn as a blue-white sweep with a crackling edge, then a white streak with one bolt from its tip.

Change: Look: both halves with the shared effect.

How it differs for the player

  • The spear's lane is drawn, so he can see what a thrust will hit before it lands.
  • A creature off to the side is no longer speared.

Risks

  • A narrow lane: many dry thrusts unless he lines up. The ±15° assist is the comfort margin.
  • Ironwood is free from the start (pass 132): many new players meet this weapon early.

Risks across the game

  • Difficulty. Sundown and Nightfall are Garry's own; the Dust Bowl and the Blood Moon were rewritten in pass 133 (BALANCING 74) on today's auto-aim. Shots that miss lower the real damage, so every stage gets harder for a poor aimer. A guess before measuring: 15 to 35% less damage dealt for a careless player, close to none for a good one.
  • Ring spawns. Garry challenges the player with a ring every 2.5 to 3.5 minutes. A forward aim clears a ring one side at a time. Rings will be the hardest moments; the sim must report deaths in rings, and their size may need to come down (Q12).
  • Boss fights. The boss is big, close and inside the barrier (18.9 m), so it is easy to face. But dodging bullet heaven turns him away from the boss, so DPS drops while he dodges. Boss HP is set from the build's full DPS (boss_hp_scaling "seconds"), which does not know about misses: bosses get relatively tougher. Measure boss fight length before and after.
  • Items and Cards. The Hydra's extra projectiles fan round the aimed shot (good). Ricochet, Trick Shot and the chains keep jumping anywhere (a reward, keep). Steady Hand pays for standing still, which fixes his facing: it needs R1's turn-on-the-spot. The Iron Horse already runs down his line. The Undertaker's ghost and Personal Storm keep their own aim. The Pocket Bible and Lightning in a Bottle do not care.
  • Outlaw identity. Calavera (Guitarra, 6 m) and Ironwood (Spear, narrow lane, free from the start) carry the most aim-dependent starting weapons; the Drifter's Revolver is the most forgiving. May's Trigger Happy needs new words.
  • The Trail's numbers. The power number (pass 83) is worked out from the build's sheet: it assumes every hit lands. The Trail's power curve (×1.39 at Trail Level 20 and so on) stays true on paper and drifts in play. Do not change the Trail until the sim has measured how much aim costs; then decide whether the power number gets an aim factor.
  • Analytics. Damage per weapon (weapon_sources) will fall and look like a nerf. The run record needs the switch (settings.aim) and a dry-shot count per weapon, so the dashboard can tell a miss from a weak weapon (run record schema 7).
  • Replays. The facing comes from the recorded stick (Lockstep.q2), so the aim line replays exactly. Placed spots must come from a new dice stream (Dice.rng_for("aim")), never the global randf. Ties in the score break by creature index. A replay proof (as pass 114's) before shipping.
  • The compiled crowd. The target picks (priority_index, nearest_index, densest_point) are script, not in native/src/crowd_core.cpp. The cone pick is new script in EnemyManager and changes nothing in the walker's path, so the native proof is not needed. If the pick costs too much later and moves into the library, then it is.
  • Performance. Dry shots mean more rounds alive in quiet stretches (cheap moments). The cone pick filters indices_in_radius by angle, a little cheaper than today's full-circle pick. The melee effects are a few meshes. Measure with perf_late before and after.
  • Feel. The Outlaw is painted in five views mirrored to eight; the aim follows the true angle, so a shot may leave 20° off the way his figure faces. The aim wedge carries the truth.

How to roll it out

Data first, one switch. Every weapon (and its evolution, and any mutation that changes it) gets an params.aim block: family, cone, hold, big_cone, fan, best_chance. One helper, core/systems/Aim.gd, replaces FireForward.gd: it reads the facing, the cone, the score and the placed spots, and every behaviour asks it at every pull (the way pass 95 asked one helper, but for all 24). A switch Settings.aim_mode (off = today) in the developer menu and the run record; the Level Editor shows the aim block on the weapon.

1The rule, the wedge and the bot. Aim.gd, the aim wedge, R1's turn-on-the-spot, and the bot's attack lean. The sim on the old rule must match today's numbers. 2The guns. Revolver, Tommy Gun, Boomstick, Basketball, Frisbee, Tumbleweed: one code path (ProjectileEmitter, Frisbee). Sim before and after; a build for Garry with the switch on. 3Melee as effects. The Sabre's arc and the Spear's streak, the blade models hidden. Captures for Garry before a build: this is where pass 95 went wrong. 4Placed. Dynamite, Molotov, Skull Rain (one Lobber change), Sun Scepter, Zap Beam, Hammer, Land Mine, Turret Buddy. 5The rest of the aimed. Big Mouth (steered beam), Guitarra, Gravity Gun, Rocket Pod, Killer Bees; Dragon's Breath only gets its data. 6Tune and decide. The rings and the late stages if the sim says so; Garry plays; the switch becomes the default for everyone, or not.

How to measure. sim_batch with 10 players, for the Drifter and Calavera, at Trail Levels quarter and half, on every stage, with the switch off and on: time alive, HP lost a minute, kills a minute, DPS per weapon, dry shots per weapon, deaths in rings, boss fight length. The difficulty probe at fixed builds (stage 3 and 4, level 30) with the bot's aim at 0.3 and 0.8. perf_late for the cost. A replay proof for determinism.

Questions for Garry

  1. Standing still: keep the last facing, and add turn-on-the-spot?Yes to both. A stick nudge under 15% turns him without walking, so standing builds can aim.
  2. How wide is "roughly"?60° for guns, the swing's own width for melee, a 100° fan for placed weapons. Narrower (40°) asks more skill; try 60° first.
  3. Do all weapons fire when nothing is in front, the Boomstick too? In pass 53 you asked the Boomstick not to.Yes for all but the Dragon's Breath, the Gravity Gun and a short wait for the Big Mouth; the Boomstick's dry blast at half volume and without the screen kick.
  4. Placed weapons: a fan ahead, or a ring all round leaning to the front?The fan (±50°). It is what "in the direction they are facing" says, and it shows on the sand.
  5. The Hammer: keep the 3D hammer landing ahead, or a hammer of light like the melee effects?A hammer of light, so all three heavy hitters read alike; the model as the fallback if it looks thin.
  6. Specials, Elites and the boss: only when roughly in front (±45°), or from any side as today (pass 73)?Only in front. Facing the Elite is the control you asked for; the boss arrow already shows where it is.
  7. Which weapons keep aiming by themselves?Orbit Saws and Salt (they do not aim), the Turret Buddy's own gun, the Tarantula Hawk, the chains and ricochets, the Undertaker's ghost. These are the soft spots for a player who struggles.
  8. The PC: keys only, or mouse aim?Keys only for players, a mouse row in the developer menu for testing.
  9. The aim wedge on the sand: on by default?On, with a Settings switch.
  10. Players' choice: a Settings row "Auto aim / Aim where I face", or one rule for everyone?One rule once it is tuned (balance once, analytics comparable). During the trial, the developer switch only.
  11. May's Trigger Happy: rework or retire?Rework: the stream stays and sways ±12° by itself.
  12. Rings in the Dust Bowl and the Blood Moon: may they be softened if the sim shows deaths cluster in them?Yes, row by row in the Level Editor, after the sim, with your sign-off.
  13. Which first?The guns (phase 2) as the first build you play, with the melee captures (phase 3) shown to you as pictures in the same pass.
